title: fix: preserve publication for new managed children
body: Closes #171782. ## What Problem This Solves A parent session outside a publishable repository can create a managed child whose tool policy permits GitHub publication, yet the child permanently loses `github_publish`. The inherited allowlist is captured from the parent's available tools after workspace discovery has omitted the publisher. The child's valid managed worktree cannot recover that missing name. ## User Impact New children retain permitted publication when the parent cannot publish from its own workspace. The child still needs an eligible workspace and must pass the Gateway's publication checks. Existing children keep their recorded policy; this change does not retroactively widen them. Explicit denies and restrictive profile, sender, sandbox, runtime, and inherited policies continue to apply. Publication credentials remain on the Gateway, and the parent's unavailable publisher stays hidden. Default sandbox allowances, publication destinations, PR editing, and merge permissions are unchanged by this PR. ## Why This Change Was Made The capture owner now passes the real unavailable publisher definition through the existing parent policy pipeline before recording the child ceiling. It removes that definition from the parent's returned tools and cron authority. The built-in runner carries the permitted definition through its later capture refresh, including the final runtime restriction, so bundled-tool preparation cannot erase it again. Native harnesses use the same capture owner. Worker-hosted turns retain the approved capture inside the Gateway turn runtime and apply later prompt restrictions before child creation; the worker catalog and parent execution grant remain unchanged. This repairs the producer and callers of the inherited snapshot without changing the stored policy format or adding a tool-name exemption. The delegation documentation explains the distinction between parent workspace availability and inherited permission. ## Evidence The baseline production-boundary reproduction failed because the eligible child lacked the publisher; explicit-deny and restrictive-allowlist controls passed. The corrected case also covers an inherited runtime restriction. Separate existing harness cases exercise host-owned availability and the built-in finalization refresh, including exclusion from parent tools and cron authority. Remote validation passed formatting, source lint, all selected production/test type graphs, the full runtime build, and 17 native test plans covering 68 files: **827 tests passed, 3 Windows-only cases skipped on Linux**. The selected tests include the unchanged publication requester and session-access owners, covering role revocation and foreign-session refusal. The test stage took 2,341 seconds including cold runtime preparation; the full runtime build accounted for 1,811 seconds. That head’s CI passed in 628 wall seconds (8,814 aggregate job seconds). The worker regression also fails on the prior implementation at the actual child-creation policy boundary. The correction has **211 passing cases across nine affected files**, including policy denial, initial and later prompt restrictions, runtime closure, and existing requester/turn revocation paths. The changed worker file’s `pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-session-tool-executor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` run took 72.29 seconds (40 cases). Formatting, lint and affected type checks pass. Independent review is complete. The native same-session scenario passed on both the exact CI base and the exact CI merge. Its original CI shard also passed all four targets on one diagnostic rerun (932 seconds); the initial discovery failure is retained as an unreproduced episode, without claiming a source fix. The remaining CI mock-export ratchet failure reproduces on the unchanged CI base and is repaired by [the upstream isolation annotation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/255c4d47a333f5bc666844e77d707ebf464c881b). The ratchet passes on the target containing that repair. A local guest parent with no publishable workspace created a fresh managed child, yielded, and received the child’s successful draft publication result. The shared publisher supplied verified human credit. An existing child remained restricted by its recorded inherited policy. Merge, automatic-merge, and repository-override requests were rejected at the request boundary before publication. The live evidence below uses the stated composed source. The later correction also requests the same private capture for unrestricted worker parents; for the restrictive guest policy shown here, the original condition already held and the behavior is unchanged. Worker behavior is verified separately through production preparation, runtime, and child-creation boundaries. The factory test supplies workspace-availability facts and does not itself claim a GitHub write. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Prior new child reports github\_publish unavailable and no publication](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97fc192d-5f44-4a9d-b24c-e8a6fe2820c8) | ![Different newly created child reports successful draft PR \#3 to the parent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2cf7240-664b-453e-9dcd-60f24f7a2004) | ### Parent submits a new\-child request, waits through delegation and receives draft PR \#3 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ba0a93a-706d-4556-b192-14ec646338c9 ### Visual verification - Baseline: d548d4d5af14be301420ee879c1a22cd0f88d607 - Exact head: `d831f0cacd27ca714761ae071451bb61ca09223c` - Scenario: An existing nonpublishing guest parent creates a new visible worktree child, yields, and automatically receives its successful shared\-publisher draft result\. - Runtime/build: Actual composed d831 runtime includes inheritance051a2ddf38245796b5aee49372f5fcdb7e3fec65; the four changed local production owners/callers are identical\. This is not a full PR\-head test\. - Controlled child difference: Before: prior new child denied\. After: a different newly created child succeeds\. Existing child permissions are not retroactively changed\. - Publisher prerequisite: Before used explicit alsoAllow; after uses the fixed default\. Both provide the effective allowed\-publisher prerequisite\. - Old\-child control: Retained owner\-mediated diagnostic still excludes publisher through inherited tools; not a second guest\-model run\. - Result: New child creates INHERITED\_PUBLISH\_SMOKE\.md and draft PR \#3; parent receives result automatically\. - Media framing: Same main\-chat crop 970×852; composer preserved so the actual submission is visible\. - Existing captures only; original files unchanged\. - Header/sidebar and model labels excluded or masked; account initials tracked and masked; child task with private identity details is outside public clip\. - Same parent and guest role; new child and allowed\-publisher configuration difference stated explicitly\. - Local composed\-source execution only; worker\-adapter qualification is separate\.
